welcome.title: Welcome, {{name}}
welcome.subtitle: Stroppy Cloud brings up databases in your cloud, drives load against them and compares the results.
welcome.verifyBody: We mailed you a code. If someone invited you to a tenant, the invite applies right after you confirm.
welcome.notInvited: Nobody invited me — create my tenant
welcome.invitedTitle: You are already on a team:
welcome.createBody: A tenant is your team's space: tests, runs, cloud providers and members. Invite colleagues later.
welcome.demo: See what a result looks like

database.title: Database
database.body: Which DBMS, version and topology: single node, replicas, cluster.
database.more: The database: DBMS (PostgreSQL, MySQL, YDB, CockroachDB…), version, topology (single node, replicas, a Patroni or Galera cluster) and its parameters. One database serves many tests.

workload.title: Workload
workload.body: What to run: Stroppy scenarios (TPC-C, TPC-H…) in segments.
workload.more: What to load and for how long: stroppy scenarios in segments — say, data load, then TPC-C at 64 VU for 10 minutes. A workload does not depend on the database and is reused.

test.title: Test
test.body: Database + workload + machine sizes. This is what you launch.
test.more: A database and a workload, plus machine sizes per role and a default provider. A test is checked up front: does the hardware meet each role's requirements.

run.title: Run
run.body: A stand comes up in the cloud, the load runs, everything is live.
run.more: One launch of a test: the stand comes up in the cloud, the database is laid out and checked, the load runs. Logs, metrics and QPS are live.

results.title: Results
results.body: QPS, latency, errors, charts; compare and rate.
results.more: What a run leaves: a report with metrics, comparison with other runs, a place in the tenant or public rating, a public link to the overview.

suite.title: Suite
suite.body: A matrix of tests and sizes — compare variants in one go.
suite.more: A matrix: several tests × size or version variants. Launched with one button, its results line up in one comparison table.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.body: Runs a test or a suite on a cron.
schedule.more: Launches a test or a suite on cron — for regular measurements and regressions. Each launch is an ordinary run with its own report.

provider.title: Provider
provider.body: Your cloud (Yandex Cloud, AWS): stands come up in it.
provider.more: Your Yandex Cloud or AWS account. A run's machines are created there and removed afterwards; you pay the cloud directly.

tenant.title: Tenant
tenant.body: Your team's space: everything above lives in it.
tenant.more: The team's space: members and roles, providers, the library, runs and limits — all of it lives in a tenant.

concepts.hint: Hover a block to see what it is and how it works.

tests.title: Tests
tests.body: The core: test = database + workload + sizes. Benchmarks start here.

runs.title: Runs
runs.body: Every run: live view, logs, metrics and results.

workloads.title: Workloads
workloads.body: Stroppy scenarios that run against databases.

suites.title: Suites
suites.body: Test matrices — compare several variants in one run.

examples.title: Examples
examples.body: Ready databases, workloads and tests: clone and run.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Cloud providers, members, limits and webhooks of the tenant.

search.title: Search
search.body: Runs, tests, databases by name. Shortcut — /.

tenant.title: Tenant
tenant.body: Switch between tenants or create a new one.

userMenu.title: Your menu
userMenu.body: Profile, theme, language. You can take this tour again from here.

empty.runs: A run is one execution of a test: a cloud stand, the load, metrics and a result. Runs appear when you launch a test or a suite.
empty.tests: A test is a database, a workload and machine sizes together. Start from an example — it is set up — or build one from your databases and workloads.
empty.databases: A database is a DBMS definition: engine, version, topology and configs. Tests reference it; a test can also define its database inline.
empty.workloads: A workload is Stroppy scenarios (TPC-C, TPC-H…) in segments: what to run, how hard and for how long.
empty.suites: A suite is a matrix of tests and sizes: several variants in one run, easy to compare.
empty.schedules: A schedule runs a test or a suite on a cron — e.g. nightly, to catch regressions.
